Trying to not have this enabled in the unit tests. Wonder if there is a better way.

ok. looks like phosphor-logging is doing something similar:
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-logging/blob/master/log_manager.cpp#L283C9-L283C21
Used a extern bool like phosphor-logging. But stayed away from creating yet another file.

Currently, pldmd does not directly create the log. It triggers asserted/de-asserted threshold alarm signal such as `criticalHighAlarmDeasserted` , Phosphor-sel-logger will watch these signal then create the SEL log.
There is new event-logging solution from Patrick, https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/event-logging.md. Does the adding code follow that solution?
@thu@os.amperecomputing.com yes! This is added to support those logs as per @patrick@stwcx.xyz's event logging design.
Acknowledged
Please Use lg2 for error, warning message.
Ugh. sorry. This slipped through my review. Thanks for catching it.
Acknowledged
Use lg2 error.
Acknowledged

Should we add the option to enable or disable this log?
After this code there is two logs (different style) for one threshold log.

We formally support log filtering in phosphor-logging now. I was considering making it easier for platforms to turn this off. That is one direction we can go in: 

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-logging/+/81041/1/tools/phosphor-logging/sensor-thresholds-eventfilter.json

Beside phosphor-logging,  phosphor-sel-logger is also used to monitor the threshold alarm to create SEL log.
So create filter in phosphor-logging is not enough I think.
Oh, I forgot about this.

There are two paths to take.
(1) For folks who want the old phosphor-sel-logger logs, they can install filters like https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-logging/+/81041/1/tools/phosphor-logging/sensor-thresholds-eventfilter.json to remove all the new logs from services. While I am clearly for the new logs, I can sympathize platform owners who have their products in prod and might not have the luxury to control the tooling above BMC.

(2) For folks who want the new logs, they can go ahead and remove "log-threshold" from phosphor-sel-logger PACKAGECONFIG
```
PACKAGECONFIG:remove = "log-threshold"
```
This is what I decided to go with for the platforms I support.

I am not fully against adding a compile time option; probably have it on by default?
Oh, I understand your idea now. `pldmd` still calls lg2::commit() but the service `phosphor-logging` handle `lg2::commit` will filter it.
I think we should not add variable in code for unit-test purpose.
Sorry. I could not find another way to keep the unit tests happy and not expect services. I am open to suggestions.
I tried to removed PLDM_THRESHOLD_LOGGING and run unit-test locally. I don't see the build error.

ohhh let me try again. Probably something has changed since I last tried it. This would be awesome if it works without this. You might see a temp #if0d commit from me to test this out, please ignore that.
Acknowledged
IN above logic, the threshold log will only be printed when the `alarm == newAlarm`. But this condition only check `newAlarm`. Can you detail more about this?
we return early and dont print anything if alarm == newAlarm (line 913).
Acknowledged

As my understanding, when there is newAlarm, `createThresholdLog` will be called to update `assertedLog`.
Which code will log to journal? in this condition?
Its createThresholdLog which will call lg2::commit(). lg2::commit will create a new phospor-logging entry and I have noticed that it also creates a journal entry.
Can you point out the code? In `createThresholdLog` I only see `lg2::error` bug not lg2::commit().

Sorry, that part of the code is a bit obtuse.
```
        auto log = thresholdEventMap.at(
            {level, direction})(sensorObjPath, value, sensorUnit, threshold);
```
calls one of the functions defined in line 999 which maps {level,direction} to a function. Each of the functions, is an implementation of the template logThresholdHelper(). And thats the one calling lg2::commit().

That avoids me from repeating the same code with different exceptions from sdbusplus::error::xyz::openbmc_project::sensor::Threshold

I should throw some comments there.
Acknowledged
When `createThresholdLog(level, direction, value);` is not called what will be the value of `assertedLog[{level, direction}];`?

the map<>'s [] operator would create a default if there is no value for the provided key. Since the default constructor for the value/std::optional is std::nullopt, the subsequent log.has_value() would return false.
Acknowledged

Acknowledged

Acknowledged

Apply the same for others logs.
